entry.title: A hug can be offered
entry.summary: Offer affection and notice whether it is welcome. Davies gives children a say in ordinary touch while keeping the adult’s responsibility to protect them.
entry.cue: A child pulls away from a hug, or your enthusiastic toddler approaches another child.
detail: When a child withdraws, you can help the other child notice: they may not want a hug just now. Davies suggests checking rather than demanding affection.

She applies the same respect to adults offering hugs or elective help. Necessary care and immediate protection still call for gentle adult action; a child’s refusal does not remove that responsibility.
